data.name: S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)
data.description: Universal methyl donor whose level reports methionine availability. SAM binds SAMTOR, which otherwise inhibits mTORC1 through the GATOR1-KICSTOR complex.
data.description_beginner: A universal 'methyl donor' molecule whose level reflects how much of the amino acid methionine is available. It binds the sensor SAMTOR, which would otherwise keep mTORC1 suppressed.

studies.title: SAMTOR is an S-adenosylmethionine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway
studies.authors: Gu X; Orozco JM; Saxton RA; Condon KJ; Liu GY; Krawczyk PA; Scaria SM; Harper JW; Gygi SP; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Extended nutrient sensing beyond amino acids to METABOLITES: SAMTOR reads S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the cell's methyl-donor currency, linking methionine and one-carbon metabolism to mTORC1. Relevant to why methionine restriction affects aging.

relations.mechanism: S-adenosylmethionine, the cell's methyl-donor currency, binds SAMTOR and pulls it off GATOR1 - this is how methionine availability reaches mTORC1.
relations.mechanism_beginner: SAM, a byproduct of methionine, binds SAMTOR and pulls it away from GATOR1 – the proposed way the cell senses how much methionine it has. Worked out in cells; whether this sensor is what matters in a whole animal has not been shown.
relations.boundary: Single-study edge. Needs independent replication before it is treated as established.
relations.note: Only one supporting study in the corpus - flag as thin.
